resources.string:
Having stock Shizuku installed alongside ShizukuX can cause permission conflicts and app crashes. To ensure ShizukuX functions correctly, please uninstall or disable the stock Shizuku app.

You can do this via:
1. Settings -> Apps -> Shizuku -> Disable/Uninstall
2. Below buttons (if ShizukuX service is running)
3. ADB: adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 moe.shizuku.privileged.api
Stock Shizuku has been disabled successfully.
Failed to disable Stock Shizuku. Ensure ShizukuX is running or use ADB manually.
Third-party apps (like SwiftBackup) will now seamlessly detect ShizukuX.
Third-party apps that explicitly check for stock Shizuku will not detect ShizukuX. Install the lightweight Compat Hub to allow apps to detect ShizukuX.
Failed to install. Ensure ShizukuX or Root is active.
Can\'t install: a different app (e.g. stock Shizuku) is already installed as moe.shizuku.privileged.api with an incompatible signature. Uninstall it first.
Can\'t install: not enough free storage on device.
Can\'t install: Compat Hub doesn\'t support this device\'s CPU architecture.

Compat Hub is a separate package, so Android never removes it together with ShizukuX. Uninstalling it now removes the compatibility layer — apps that only check the stock Shizuku package name will report Shizuku as missing.\n\nTip: do this BEFORE uninstalling ShizukuX. Once the manager is gone, the hub keeps its own launcher icon and can still be removed from there or from system Settings → Apps.
Failed to uninstall Compat Hub. Ensure ShizukuX service or Root is active, or remove it from system Settings → Apps.
